rules.air_fuel.help: Open General: flying at all costs a minimum of one third of the aircraft's full movement in fuel, however short the hop, and an aircraft that ends its turn out of fuel with no airfield or friendly carrier on or beside its hex crashes and is lost. Forgiving: OSADA simply stops a dry aircraft moving and it sits where it is. The move overlay already accounts for the sortie minimum, so a route you can plan is a route the aircraft can finish, and every crash is listed in the turn report.
rules.air_fuel.label: Aircraft fuel model
rules.air_fuel.value.1: Minimum sortie cost; dry aircraft away from base are lost
rules.air_zoc.help: Open General 6.30 says air units usually have no zone of control - this is the exception, and each scenario decides for itself. With this on, a scenario that sets the option lets its aircraft project a zone of control like any ground formation. 79 of the 457 scenarios whose source can be read set it.
rules.air_zoc.label: Aircraft extend zones of control
rules.build_and_repair.help: Open General: engineers with the Sapper ability build bridges, fortifications, airfields and ports for prestige over several turns, and repair what was destroyed; units able to demolish blow bridges and raze terrain outright. Off: terrain is fixed for the whole scenario.
rules.build_and_repair.label: Build and repair
rules.barrage.help: Open General: a formation whose equipment can bombard (Open General marks it with '=') may shell a hex it cannot see, within its gun range. A successful barrage takes strength, ammunition, fuel and two levels of entrenchment off anything hidden there, and reduces a city, airfield, port or bridge to wreckage that costs more to cross until engineers repair it. What may be wrecked is the equipment file's decision, exactly as it is for demolition charges. The shot is spent whether or not it lands, and the scenario's author must allow it. Off: fire is only ever aimed at something you can see.
rules.barrage.label: Barrage fire
rules.carrier_deploy.help: Open General: an aircraft whose equipment allows it may be placed onto a friendly aircraft carrier when deploying, which is otherwise impossible because a ship at sea is never in a deployment zone. Purely additive - no hex you could already deploy onto stops being one.
rules.carrier_deploy.label: Deploy onto carriers
rules.craters.help: An OSADA rule, not an Open General one: a barrage that lands on open ground with nothing to wreck digs shell craters. A crater costs one extra movement point to enter, and it gives whoever holds it a floor of one entrenchment level - cover nobody had to dig. It is a floor and never a bonus, so it can never beat entrenching and shelling your own line buys you nothing. Off: shells that hit open ground do nothing to it, which is what Open General does.
rules.craters.label: Shell craters
rules.counterbattery.help: Open General: artillery with the Counterbattery ability answers enemy artillery that fires on one of your formations, once per turn. The reply is one-sided - the artillery being answered does not shoot back - and it spends the answering battery's own shot for the turn. Off: artillery is only ever answered by the unit it attacked.
rules.counterbattery.label: Counterbattery fire
rules.depot_supply.help: Open General: a supply unit acts as a mobile depot, resupplying adjacent friendly formations on better terms than the field offers - terrain and nearby enemies do not reduce it, and neither side is disqualified for having already moved or fired. The equipment file chooses which of Open General's four supply modes apply. No equipment file that ships with OSADA sets them yet, so turning this on changes nothing until content asks for it.
rules.depot_supply.label: Depot supply
rules.dry_unit_penalties.help: Open General: a unit out of ammunition defends with halved strength and halved initiative; one out of fuel has its initiative halved. OSADA already stops an empty unit attacking and a dry one moving — this adds the penalties on top of those prohibitions.
rules.dry_unit_penalties.label: Empty units fight worse
rules.equipment_toggles.help: Open General: whether a formation gets reconnaissance movement and the overrun charge is decided by its own equipment record, which can switch either on for a unit whose class would not have it or off for one whose class would. Off: the unit's class decides both, as it always has in OSADA. Turning this on changes what thousands of records can do, so it is not a cosmetic setting.
rules.equipment_toggles.label: Abilities from the record
rules.extended_los.help: Open General's extended sight rules. Mountains, hills, forest, city and bocage block sight and ranged fire past them. Troops in forest are seen by enemy ground units only from an adjacent hex, and troops in forest or city are seen from the air only within two hexes. Off: sight and fire reach anything inside range regardless of what lies between.
rules.extended_los.label: Extended line of sight
rules.extended_naval.help: Open General 9.6, as one switch because Open General treats it as one: ships return fire against artillery and forts; ships can only attack submarines from an adjacent hex; destroyers escort naval transports against submarine attacks the way fighters escort bombers; and a submarine needs a clear line of fire to attack. Two of the four take shots away - most shipped warships have a gun range above one and lose every long shot at a submarine - so this is off unless you ask for it. 238 of the 457 scenarios whose source can be read do ask for it.
rules.extended_naval.label: Extended naval rules
rules.ground_auto_supply.help: Open General resupplies any ground formation that does nothing for a whole turn and names no terrain condition. OSADA additionally requires a city hex. Relaxing it is a balance decision, not a correction: it hands every idle formation in the field a free full refit. Enemies next to the formation still block resupply under either setting, because a unit being shot at is not idle.
rules.ground_auto_supply.label: Idle ground units resupply anywhere
rules.heavy_move_fire.help: Open General: artillery and air-defence guns have to shoot before moving, because they must be unlimbered to fire. Equipment carrying the Mechanized attribute is exempt, and so is a formation with a Mechanized Veteran commander. Off: a gun may move and fire in either order, which is what OSADA has always done — turning this on changes how every artillery battery is played.
rules.heavy_move_fire.label: Guns must fire before they move
rules.initiative_model.help: What decides who reacts first. OSADA reads the equipment's own initiative, its attachments and the terrain the defender stands in, and nothing else, so the same attack always resolves the same way. Open General also counts the crews' experience — one point per completed experience bar — and adds a small random swing for the uncertainty of battle, which changes what a First Strike commander is worth. The swing is rolled only when the attack is actually made, so with this on the battle forecast becomes an estimate rather than an exact figure. Both players in a network game roll the same swing.
rules.initiative_model.label: Combat initiative
rules.installation_spotting.help: Open General: a city, port or airfield you own sees its own hex and the ones next to it even with no unit in the garrison. Off: only units see. Vision follows ownership, so a town changing hands changes who can see from it in the same turn.
rules.installation_spotting.label: Cities and airfields watch
rules.minefields.help: Open General's land minefields: fields the scenario author placed, plus fields laid during play by units able to drop mines and cleared by units able to remove them. Entering a minefield you have detected costs the rest of your movement; entering one you have not also costs strength. A unit standing in a minefield has one movement point and reduced defence. Off: no minefield exists, nothing has to be laid or cleared, and any field a scenario authored is ignored.
rules.minefields.label: Minefields
rules.naval_critical_hits.help: Open General: a naval shot can sink its target outright. The chance rises with the firing unit's naval attack, experience and strength, falls with the target's defence and strength, is capped at 75%, and submarines add 10% whenever they are the ones firing. The equipment file supplies the multiplier - Open General's own eqp-lxf sets it to 2, and OSADA has never applied it. Off unless you ask for it: it sinks ships regardless of how much strength they have left.
rules.naval_critical_hits.label: Naval critical hits
rules.provenance.scenario_authored: Chosen by this scenario's own settings
rules.rail_transport.help: Open General: a ground formation standing on a railway may be sent along connected track to another boarding point, spending one of its player's rail transport points. A station is needed at both ends unless the formation can board anywhere. 120 scenarios grant a rail transport pool; the rest are unaffected.
rules.carrier_hangars.help: Open General: aircraft ride INSIDE a carrier rather than parked on its deck — out of sight, out of reach, and out of the way of the hex's one air slot. A ship carries as many as its own record allows, an aircraft cannot take off again on the turn it landed, and a hangar goes down with its ship. Only equipment files that enable carriers offer it.
rules.carrier_hangars.label: Carrier hangars
rules.green_replacements.help: Open General: a second, cheaper way to bring a battered formation back up to strength — raw recruits instead of trained replacements. They cost a fraction of the usual price and dilute the unit's experience, and under some equipment files a commander leaves when his formation loses its last experience bar this way. Only equipment files that define green replacements offer it.
rules.green_replacements.label: Green replacements
rules.rail_transport.label: Railway transport
rules.replacement_experience.label: Replacements dilute experience
rules.replacement_experience.help: Diluted: fresh replacements arrive untrained, so a formation's experience becomes the strength-weighted average of its veterans and its new intake — a formation at strength 3 with 400 experience rebuilt to 10 keeps 120. Combat reads whole experience bars of 100, so a small top-up may cost nothing in effect. Preserved: replacements never reduce experience, which is what OSADA did before. Overstrength is never diluted, and a commander's own experience is separate and never touched.
rules.snow_fuel.help: Open General: a unit normally spends one point of fuel per movement point, except in snow, where it spends two. The move overlay already accounts for it, so a route you can plan is a route the unit can finish.
rules.snow_fuel.label: Snow doubles fuel use
rules.snow_fuel.value.1: Two fuel per movement point in snow
rules.spotting_memory.help: Open General: a hex your side has seen this turn stays visible until your turn ends, so a reconnaissance element can find a target and drive on without the target disappearing again. Live: visibility follows your units hex by hex, which is what OSADA has always done. The memory is dropped when your turn ends, so it never shows you where the enemy moved on their own turn.
rules.spotting_memory.label: Spotted hexes stay spotted
rules.support_fire_range_falloff.help: Open General: a unit adjacent to the one being attacked supports at full strength; anything further away supports at half. Distance is measured to the unit under attack, not to the attacker, so a battery in depth supports at half however close the assault gets to its own hex. Off: every eligible supporter fires at full strength.
rules.support_fire_range_falloff.label: Distant supporting fire is halved
rules.support_fire_range_falloff.value.1: Half unless adjacent to the defender

equipment.ability.allow_lof: Allows Line of Fire: this formation never blocks a friendly line of fire. It matters only in scenarios where units block fire at all; elsewhere nothing blocks it and the ability changes nothing.
equipment.ability.anti_sub: ASW (Anti-Submarine Warfare): may attack submarines, like a Destroyer or Tactical Bomber.
equipment.ability.bridge: Bridge: acts as a bridge when standing in a river hex, letting other units cross.
equipment.ability.build_repair: Sapper: can build a bridge, fortification, airfield or port, and repair what was destroyed.
equipment.ability.can_air_attack: Can Attack Air: may attack aircraft despite not being an anti-air class.
equipment.ability.can_blow: Can Blow: can demolish the bridge it stands on, or raze the terrain feature of its hex.
equipment.ability.cannot_attack_air: Cannot attack aircraft, regardless of its air attack value.
equipment.ability.cannot_attack_naval: No Naval Attack: this equipment has no weapon that can engage a ship, whatever its naval attack value says.
equipment.ability.cant_buy: Cannot Be Bought: never available for purchase. It reaches the field only as a scenario unit or an authored reinforcement.
equipment.ability.no_ai_buy: Not Bought By The AI: available to you, but the computer opponent will never purchase it. It is usually equipment an author reserves for the player's side.
equipment.ability.no_prototype: No Prototype: cannot be one of the early prototypes a brilliant victory awards, even when it is otherwise in date.
equipment.ability.air_transportable: Air Transportable: may be carried by an air transport. A prime mover without it is left behind on the airfield when its formation is airlifted.
equipment.ability.capture_flag: Capture: may capture flagged objective hexes.
equipment.ability.carrier_deploy: Carrier Deploy: may be deployed onto a friendly aircraft carrier, which is otherwise outside any deployment zone.
equipment.ability.clear_mines: Clear Mines: can attempt to clear a land minefield while standing in it; a failed attempt suppresses it.
equipment.ability.cut_los: Cuts Line of Sight: blocks ranged fire passing through this unit's hex, for both sides. Sight itself is not blocked.
equipment.ability.counter_battery: Counterbattery: answers enemy artillery that fires on a friendly formation within range, once per turn.
equipment.ability.dismount: Dismount: reverses whether this unit fights with its own statistics when attacked while riding a transport, instead of its transport's.
equipment.ability.dismount_after_move: Dismount After Move: steps down from its transport automatically once its move ends, instead of riding until next turn.
equipment.ability.drop_mines: Drop Mines: can lay a land minefield on its own hex - 2 ammunition, and no other action that turn.
equipment.ability.evade: Evade: has a 50% chance of evading any attack, like a submarine.
equipment.ability.exploit_success: Exploit Success: may move again after an attack that kills or routs the defender.
equipment.ability.ignores_entrenchment: Ignores Entrenchment: attacking this unit gets no benefit from the defender's entrenchment level.
equipment.ability.jet_stealth: Jet (Stealth): marked on jet aircraft; its exact effect is not documented anywhere, so do not assume one from the name.
equipment.ability.kamikaze: Kamikaze: may sacrifice itself in a suicide attack.
equipment.ability.lasting_suppression: Lasting Suppression: suppression it inflicts lasts until the end of the enemy's turn instead of clearing at the round wrap.
equipment.ability.marine: Marine: trained for amphibious assault - keeps its movement after landing from a naval transport, instead of coming ashore spent.
equipment.ability.mechanized: Mechanized: the crew rides its own prime mover, so the gun is exempt from having to fire before it moves.
equipment.ability.mountain: Mountain: mountain-trained, so hills, rough ground and the mountains themselves cost it no more than dedicated mountain infantry pays.
equipment.ability.no_ammo_penalty: No Ammo Penalty: does not suffer the usual penalty for defending without ammunition.
equipment.ability.no_dirt_airfields: Cannot use dirt airfields: cannot refuel or deploy at an airfield defined as dirt, or one built by sappers during the scenario.
equipment.ability.no_intercept_air: No Intercept Air: does not intercept aircraft moving through its range, though it still defends normally when attacked.
equipment.ability.no_leader: No Leader: this equipment never produces a commander.
equipment.ability.no_need_station: No Need Station: can board and leave a train anywhere on the track, with no railway station at either end.
equipment.ability.rail_transportable: Rail Transportable: this formation may be carried by train. Emplaced anti-aircraft and permanent fortifications mostly cannot be.
equipment.ability.no_surrender: No Surrender: never destroyed-as-surrendered when a forced retreat is impossible — fights on in place instead.
equipment.ability.no_zoc: No Zone of Control: this unit does not slow or stop enemy formations moving past it.
equipment.ability.partizan: Partizan: fights in its own country's forests and villages and cannot be caught by surprise.
equipment.ability.rocket_bomber: Rocket Bomber: attacks ground targets at its full range rather than a reduced one.
equipment.ability.single_fire_sup: Single Fire Support: may give support fire only once per turn.
equipment.ability.supply_unit: Supply Unit: acts as a mobile depot, resupplying adjacent friendly formations even if they have already moved or fired.
equipment.ability.torpedo_bomber: Torpedo Bomber: attacks an adjacent unit with torpedoes if both are at sea.
equipment.ability.all_weather: All Weather: not affected by weather — attacks, is attacked, and spots normally regardless of conditions.

tutorial.command.body:
Well done, Commander.

The three-turn demonstration is complete. The next Soviet turn is yours.

Capture the Hamar-Daba Command Post to win. Bain-Tsagan Observation Point is optional.

Scout first, soften entrenched defenders with artillery, and use armour to exploit the breach.
tutorial.command.title: You Are Now in Command
tutorial.turn1.complete: The first demonstration turn is complete. A scenario is lost if its primary objectives are not taken before the final turn shown on the top bar.
tutorial.turn1.hamar_daba: Hamar-Daba is the second primary objective. Both primary objectives must be held to win, and capturing them awards prestige for reinforcement, upgrades, and new units.
tutorial.turn1.optional_objective: Bain-Tsagan Observation Point is optional: it is not required for victory, but it offers extra prestige, experience, and a useful forward position.
tutorial.turn1.primary_crossing: Primary objectives have an enemy flag inside a golden frame. Capture this crossing by moving one of your ground units onto the hex after its defender has been removed.
tutorial.turn1.recon: The BA-10 is a reconnaissance unit. Recon has a larger spotting range and may move in several stages, making it ideal for revealing ambushes before slower units advance.
tutorial.turn1.strength: The number beside a unit is its strength. It represents how much of the formation remains combat-effective. The colour and small status markers also show whether the unit has moved or fired during the current turn.
tutorial.turn1.terrain: Roads are usually fastest, while hills, rivers, marshes, and rough ground reduce movement in different ways. Scout first, then commit the tanks and infantry.
tutorial.turn1.transport:
This machine-gun battalion has truck transport. Press the truck button to mount or dismount it: [
Transport greatly improves movement on roads, but mounted units are vulnerable. Infantry automatically dismounts when attacked.
tutorial.turn1.unit_info: Selecting a unit opens its Unit Info card in the lower-left corner. Press ALL STATS to expand movement, spotting, attack, defence, ammunition, fuel, experience, and entrenchment. Highlighted hexes show the unit’s current movement range.
tutorial.turn2.artillery: The crossing is held by entrenched infantry. Artillery attacks from range, normally avoids return fire, and reduces entrenchment — this is artillery preparation or softening.
tutorial.turn2.bombardment: That was a real bombardment: the defender lost strength and/or entrenchment, ammunition was spent, and both formations gained combat experience. Prepared positions should be softened before a close assault.
tutorial.turn2.combat_estimate: Before attacking, the combat cursor estimates losses for both sides. Treat the estimate as a warning rather than a promise: terrain, experience, entrenchment, initiative, and support fire can all change the result.
tutorial.turn2.counterattack: The Japanese counterattack forced the transported infantry to dismount automatically. The nearby Soviet battery also provided support fire: artillery may fire automatically when a friendly ground unit inside its range is attacked.
tutorial.turn2.target_types: Infantry and artillery are soft targets; tanks are hard targets. Different weapons use different attack values against them. The BT-5 is now positioned to exploit the weakened line next turn.
tutorial.turn3.crossing_captured: Khaylastyn Crossing has been captured. The flag changes to your side and the prestige award is added to the top bar. Early objective captures also improve the final score.
tutorial.turn3.overrun_result: OverRun! The weakened unit was destroyed and the BT-5 remains able to continue its advance. OverRun is the reward for preparing the attack and committing armour at the right moment.
tutorial.turn3.overrun_setup: The artillery preparation has left the forward company at breaking point. A tank attacking an adjacent unit can score an OverRun when it destroys the defender while suffering no more than one loss.
tutorial.turn3.reinforcement: Reinforcement restores lost strength and costs prestige. Enemy units nearby reduce the result, and a reinforced unit cannot move or attack again during that turn.
tutorial.turn3.resupply: Units consume ammunition and, when motorised, fuel. A unit without ammunition cannot attack, and a motorised unit without fuel cannot move. Press the barrel button to restore both: !
tutorial.welcome.body:
Tutorial — Khalkhin Gol
3 July 1939
Japanese forces have crossed the Khalkhin Gol and occupied positions around the Bain-Tsagan heights. The first three turns are an AI-controlled demonstration of objectives, unit information, transport, reconnaissance, artillery preparation, support fire, reinforcement, resupply, and OverRun. At the start of turn 4, full control of the Soviet-Mongolian detachment passes to you. Capture the Khaylastyn Crossing and the Hamar-Daba Command Post; the Bain-Tsagan Observation Point is optional.
